title: Cheese spread, American or Cheddar cheese base

content.title: About
content.content: Cheese spread is a smooth, creamy paste made from melted American or Cheddar cheese. It has a rich buttery flavor with a mild tang typical of Cheddar. The product is commonly used as a spread, dip, or ingredient in various dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: American cheese was created in the early 20th century to extend the shelf life of traditional cheeses.
Cheddar originated in England’s Cheddar region in the 12th century and is now one of the world’s most popular cheeses.
Cheese spreads often contain small amounts of emulsifiers and stabilizers to keep a uniform texture.
In the United States, American‑cheese‑based spreads are a staple in fast‑food burgers and sandwiches.
There are many flavor variations: herb‑infused, spicy, smoked, or blended with blue‑cheese crumbles.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Cheese spread provides calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Protein from the cheese helps maintain muscle mass and promotes satiety.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamins B2 and B12, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Phosphorus content
items.content: Phosphorus contributes to cellular function and energy production.

items.title: Potential probiotic cultures
items.content: Some fermented cheese spreads may contain beneficial bacteria for gut health.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Cheese spreads are often salty, which can be an issue for people with hypertension.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: They contain saturated fats that may affect cholesterol levels.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The product contains lactose, so those with intolerance should choose lactose‑free versions.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to casein or whey may react to cheese spread.

items.title: Additives
items.content: Commercial varieties may include preservatives and emulsifiers that can cause sensitivities in some consumers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Spread it on bread, crackers, or vegetable sticks, use as a burger topping, stir into sauces, casseroles, or potato dishes. It also pairs well with fruits, nuts, or as a dip for chips.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the spread refrigerated at 2‑4 °C in its original packaging or an airtight container. Once opened, consume within 5‑7 days. Discard if it develops off‑odors, discoloration, or mold.
